# OPERAVA MailDesk — LLM Implementation Reference

This file is the machine-readable source of truth for coding agents working in this repository.

## Authority

Follow the current source code and database migration. Do not invent routes, tables, UI features, integrations, or deployment workflows that are not present.

## Product

OPERAVA MailDesk is a secure, garden-themed internal email workspace.

Brand asset: operava_exact_transparent.png

## Current stack

- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend
- Supabase Auth for email/password authentication
- Cloudflare Worker API
- Supabase Postgres + RLS
- Resend API for server-side email delivery
- Signed Resend webhook ingestion
- Cloudflare Pages for static frontend hosting

## Browser routes

- / redirects to /login
- /login serves login_page.html
- /mailbox serves mailbox.html
- /backend serves operava-maildesk-backend-stack.html

There is one login experience only. Do not add a second login form to the mailbox.

## Authentication

Supabase Auth is the only authentication authority.

Login:
1. Browser sends email/password to the Supabase Auth password token endpoint.
2. Successful authentication returns a Supabase session.
3. The session is stored as operava-maildesk-session.
4. Browser redirects to /mailbox.

Mailbox:
1. /mailbox requires operava-maildesk-session.
2. The access token is validated against Supabase Auth /auth/v1/user.
3. Invalid or missing sessions are cleared and redirected to /login.
4. Worker API calls use Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.

Logout:
1. The browser calls Supabase Auth logout when a token exists.
2. The local session is removed.
3. Browser returns to /login.

The following are forbidden authentication bypasses:
- ?auth=1
- ?logged_in=1
- fake local sessions
- operava_logged_in cookies
- /api/auth/login
- /api/auth/logout

## Frontend files

- index.html — root login entry, synchronized with login_page.html
- login_page.html — official login UI
- mailbox.html — authenticated MailDesk UI
- app.js — functional lightweight mailbox/API implementation
- app.css — shared mailbox styling
- app-config.js — public browser configuration only
- operava_exact_transparent.png — brand logo

Do not place Supabase service-role/secret keys or Resend API keys in browser files.

## Worker routes

- GET /health
- POST /webhooks/resend
- authenticated GET /emails
- authenticated POST /emails

The Worker validates the bearer token against Supabase Auth before protected routes.

## Database

Migration: supabase/migrations/0001_maildesk.sql

Objects:
- enum mailbox_status
- table emails
- table email_events

RLS is enabled. User-owned email records are restricted to authenticated users.

## Resend

Sending is performed by the Worker. Resend webhook requests are verified with the configured signing secret.

Current status mapping:
- email.sent -> sent
- email.bounced -> failed
- email.complained -> failed

Do not claim complete open/click/delivery synchronization.

## Browser configuration

app-config.js contains only:
- supabaseUrl
- supabaseAnonKey
- apiBaseUrl

Replace the placeholders with the project's public Supabase URL, browser-safe Supabase anon/publishable key, and deployed Worker URL during deployment.

Never put:
- Supabase service-role/secret key
- Resend API key
- Resend webhook secret
in app-config.js.

## Cloudflare deployment

The frontend is static and requires no framework build command.

Worker configuration: worker/wrangler.toml

Worker secrets:
- SUPABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
- SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
- RESEND_API_KEY
- RESEND_FROM
- RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
- FRONTEND_URL

## Validation

Run:
    node --check app.js
    node --check worker/src/index.js

Do not claim an end-to-end test suite exists.

## Not implemented

Do not describe these as live features unless source and schema are changed:
- boards/sticky-note workspace
- Supabase Storage attachments
- message threading
- rich-text editor
- browser Realtime subscription
- full delivered/opened/clicked tracking
- GitHub Actions deployment workflow
